<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="כסלו_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518915758_theRebbe_412" batchId="meluket-_D7_9B_D7_A1_D7_9C_D7_95_meluket__BH_POST_1766518915758_theRebbe_412__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the work of a chassid draws from the innermost aspect of Atik, above the levels of tzaddik and yashar, corresponding to chesed which is above tzedakah and wealth.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And this can be explained according to what is continued in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="2">that it is brought in the Zohar,</t>
    <t s="3">"Who is a chassid? One who acts piously with his Maker,"</t>
    <t s="4">that is, the concept of a chassid is that his service is not for himself, in order that he should be attached to Elokus, but rather for the sake of the Supernal.</t>
    <t s="5">As explained in Tanya.</t>
    <t s="6">And it is explained in the maamar,</t>
    <t s="7">that the drawing down that comes through the service of chassidim is from the innermost aspect of Atik.</t>
    <t s="8">And this is that a chassid is above a tzaddik and also above a yashar.</t>
    <t s="9">For the drawing down that comes through the service of tzaddikim is from the externality of the Kesser,</t>
    <t s="10">Arich.</t>
    <t s="11">And the drawing down that comes through the service of yesharim</t>
    <t s="12">(who are above tzaddikim)</t>
    <t s="13">is from the innerness of the Kesser,</t>
    <t s="14">Atik.</t>
    <t s="15">And the drawing down that comes through the service of chassidim</t>
    <t s="16">(who are above yesharim)</t>
    <t s="17">is from the innermost aspect of Atik.</t>
    <t s="18">For because their service is in bittul</t>
    <t s="19">(above existence),</t>
    <t s="20">therefore the drawing down that is drawn through their service is from the aspect of the Essence that is above diffusion</t>
    <t s="21">(existence),</t>
    <t s="22">the innermost aspect of Atik.</t>
    <t s="23">And this is that which our sages said,</t>
    <t s="24">that tzedakah is for the poor and gemilus chassadim is both for the poor and for the rich,</t>
    <t s="25">for from this</t>
    <t s="26">(that gemilus chassadim is also for the rich)</t>
    <t s="27">it is understood that chesed is above even wealth.</t>
    <t s="28">And it is explained,</t>
    <t s="29">that these three matters</t>
    <t s="30">(tzedakah,</t>
    <t s="31">wealth and chesed)</t>
    <t s="32">are three levels in the drawings down above that are drawn into Malchus.</t>
    <t s="33">Tzedakah, which is filling a lack</t>
    <t s="34">[enough for his lack and you are not commanded to enrich him]</t>
    <t s="35">is the drawing down of the revelation that pertains to Malchus,</t>
    <t s="36">through which its lack is filled.</t>
    <t s="37">For in this revelation is also included the aspect of the externality of the Kesser,</t>
    <t s="38">Arich.</t>
    <t s="39">For since Arich is the root and source of the emanations, except that it encompasses them</t>
    <t s="40">(Sovev),</t>
    <t s="41">it is included in the light that pertains to the worlds</t>
    <t s="42">(Malchus).</t>
    <t s="43">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="44">that the name tzaddik is from the term tzedakah,</t>
    <t s="45">for through the service of tzaddikim is the drawing down of the externality of the Kesser</t>
    <t s="46">(as above),</t>
    <t s="47">for this drawing down is included in filling a lack,</t>
    <t s="48">tzedakah.</t>
    <t s="49">And wealth,</t>
    <t s="50">which is above filling a lack,</t>
    <t s="51">is the drawing down of a revelation of light that is above relation to Malchus</t>
    <t s="52">(that is drawn into Malchus),</t>
    <t s="53">the innerness of the Kesser,</t>
    <t s="54">Atik.</t>
    <t s="55">And chesed, which is above even wealth, is the drawing down of the innermost aspect of Atik</t>
    <t s="56">(that is drawn into Malchus).</t>
    <t s="57">And this is "Who is a chassid? One who acts piously with his Maker,"</t>
    <t s="58">for the reasons for this, that one whose service is</t>
    <t s="59">(not for his own sake,</t>
    <t s="60">but rather)</t>
    <t s="61">for the sake of the Supernal is called by the name chassid</t>
    <t s="62">(from the term chesed),</t>
    <t s="63">is,</t>
    <t s="64">for because his service is in ultimate bittul</t>
    <t s="65">(above existence),</t>
    <t s="66">the drawing down through his service is from the innermost aspect of Atik</t>
    <t s="67">(as above),</t>
    <t s="68">the matter of chesed,</t>
    <t s="69">therefore he is called by the name chassid.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the blessing drawn by chassidim comes from the place of hodaa (acknowledgment) in the innermost aspect of Atik, and that the unique quality of this drawing is that it occurs in a spontaneous manner.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that what is written "They will thank You... and Your chassidim will bless You,"</t>
    <t s="3">that the superiority of the drawing down</t>
    <t s="4">(blessing)</t>
    <t s="5">that comes through "Your chassidim" is that the drawing down is from a place where comprehension does not pertain, only hodaa (acknowledgment) alone,</t>
    <t s="6">is,</t>
    <t s="7">for the true concept of hodaa is in the innermost aspect of Atik,</t>
    <t s="8">and the drawing down from there</t>
    <t s="9">(in the manner of blessing)</t>
    <t s="10">is specifically through "Your chassidim."</t>
    <t s="11">Also, it can be said,</t>
    <t s="12">that the main novelty in "They will thank You... will bless You" is,</t>
    <t s="13">that the drawing down from the place where the concept of hodaa is</t>
    <t s="14">(Ein Sof that is above Hishtalshelus)</t>
    <t s="15">is in the manner of blessing</t>
    <t s="16">("will bless You"),</t>
    <t s="17">meaning that the drawing down is in a spontaneous way,</t>
    <t s="18">and the drawing down in this manner is</t>
    <t s="19">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="20">specifically through "Your chassidim."</t>
    <t s="21">That is, that this—that the drawing down is from the place where the concept of hodaa is—</t>
    <t s="22">applies also to tzaddikim and yesharim.</t>
    <t s="23">For since even Arich, and certainly the externality of Atik, are above Hishtalshelus,</t>
    <t s="24">comprehension does not pertain to them, only hodaa alone.</t>
    <t s="25">But the drawing down from Arich and from the externality of Atik</t>
    <t s="26">(through tzaddikim and yesharim)</t>
    <t s="27">is</t>
    <t s="28">(like)</t>
    <t s="29">in the manner of action,</t>
    <t s="30">and the true concept of "in a spontaneous way" is in the drawing down from the innermost aspect of Atik</t>
    <t s="31">(through "Your chassidim"),</t>
    <t s="32">as will be explained below.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that Arich corresponds to will and Atik to delight, and that the drawing down through tzaddikim is by force of will, while through yesharim it is by the delight that transforms the very nature of the recipient.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">8)</t>
    <t s="1">And the concept is,</t>
    <t s="2">that Arich and Atik are analogous to will and delight.</t>
    <t s="3">And among the distinctions between will and delight is,</t>
    <t s="4">that the action of will upon the faculties and limbs is in a manner of domination,</t>
    <t s="5">meaning that the faculties and limbs, in and of themselves, remain in their nature as they were before, except that the will dominates them and forces them to be according to the will</t>
    <t s="6">(contrary to their nature).</t>
    <t s="7">And the action that is done in the faculties and limbs through delight,</t>
    <t s="8">since delight is the innerness and life-force of the faculties and limbs themselves,</t>
    <t s="9">therefore,</t>
    <t s="10">the action done in them through delight is</t>
    <t s="11">(not in a manner of domination and coercion,</t>
    <t s="12">but rather)</t>
    <t s="13">that they themselves become so.</t>
    <t s="14">And likewise above,</t>
    <t s="15">the change</t>
    <t s="16">(as it were)</t>
    <t s="17">that occurs in the level of Hishtalshelus through the drawing down of the externality of the Kesser that is drawn through tzaddikim,</t>
    <t s="18">that even when, from the perspective of the aspect of Hishtalshelus, there is a decree that there should not be a drawing down of influence, and through the tzaddik drawing down a new will from the Kesser that is above Hishtalshelus</t>
    <t s="19">(the externality of the Kesser)</t>
    <t s="20">the decree is nullified,</t>
    <t s="21">it is in a manner of domination and rulership</t>
    <t s="22">("A tzaddik rules in the fear of G-d"),</t>
    <t s="23">that the will that is above Hishtalshelus dominates and rules over Hishtalshelus.</t>
    <t s="24">And the nullification of the decree that comes from the aspect of Hishtalshelus through the drawing down of the innerness of the Kesser that is drawn through the service of yesharim is</t>
    <t s="25">(not in a manner of domination,</t>
    <t s="26">but rather)</t>
    <t s="27">that since the delight of the innerness of the Kesser is the innerness of Hishtalshelus,</t>
    <t s="28">therefore,</t>
    <t s="29">through the drawing down of the innerness of the will and delight</t>
    <t s="30">(of the innerness of the Kesser),</t>
    <t s="31">where the will there is that there should be influence,</t>
    <t s="32">the nullification of the decree is also from the perspective of Hishtalshelus itself.</t>
    <t s="33">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="34">that this is what our sages said,</t>
    <t s="35">"Anyone who teaches Torah to the son of an ignoramus, even if the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees a decree, He nullifies it for his sake, as it is said,</t>
    <t s="36">'And if you bring out the precious from the vile, you shall be as My mouth.'"</t>
    <t s="37">For the language "He nullifies it for his sake" indicates that the Holy One, blessed be He, nullifies it for his sake,</t>
    <t s="38">for it can be said,</t>
    <t s="39">that this is more elevated than that which is "the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees and a tzaddik nullifies."</t>
    <t s="40">And the concept is,</t>
    <t s="41">that the primary delight above is from the innovation</t>
    <t s="42">of the transformation of darkness into light,</t>
    <t s="43">to bring out the precious from the vile.</t>
    <t s="44">And since through the service of this tzaddik who teaches and disseminates Torah even to the son of an ignoramus, the delight above is generated,</t>
    <t s="45">therefore,</t>
    <t s="46">the nullification of the decree through him is</t>
    <t s="47">[not in the manner of "the Holy One, blessed be He, decrees and a tzaddik nullifies,"</t>
    <t s="48">meaning that from the perspective of the level of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="49">(Hishtalshelus)</t>
    <t s="50">there is a decree,</t>
    <t s="51">but rather through the level that is above Hishtalshelus</t>
    <t s="52">(the externality of the Kesser)</t>
    <t s="53">that is drawn through the tzaddik, which rules over the level of Hishtalshelus</t>
    <t s="54">("A tzaddik rules in the fear of G-d")</t>
    <t s="55">it is nullified,</t>
    <t s="56">but rather],</t>
    <t s="57">that through the delight</t>
    <t s="58">(the innerness of the Kesser)</t>
    <t s="59">that is generated above through his service,</t>
    <t s="60">the nullification of the decree is also from the perspective of the level of the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="61">(Hishtalshelus).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
